title: bus/daemon: one lock per scan, one bus snapshot per tick, archive old closed tasks (measured cause of minutes-long ticks)
spec:
Measured root cause of the slow daemon ticks (Planner, 2026-10-08 08:00, orchestrator repo, 1725 task files):
- bus.read() takes 2.6-5.2 s. cProfile of bus.read(status="queued"): 1725 calls to bus.get (bus.py:88), each entering
  bus.locked() (bus.py:19) and calling fcntl.flock: 2.26 s in flock alone, 0.97 s in json.loads.
- tick() and its stages call bus.read many times per tick, several inside per-task loops (e.g. daemon.py ~986
  `children = [r for r in bus.read(role="spec_review") ...]` per candidate, ~1722 the same in another loop, merge_reviewed,
  planner_runs.build_ctx `[t for t in bus.read() if t.get("parent") == goal["id"]]`). A tick therefore costs minutes and the
  restarted daemon took 20+ min for its first tick; ready tasks wait that long (luna and ai-apprentice show the same at
  ~600 and ~370 tasks).
Fix (supersedes T-1715, whose broader instrumentation is folded in as item 4):
1. bus.read() takes the lock once for the whole scan (or reads without the per-file lock: writers already write atomically
   via _save; if not, make _save write-then-rename) instead of one flock per task.
2. A per-tick snapshot: tick() reads the bus once (bus.read()) and passes/uses an in-memory index (by id, status, role,
   parent, inputs[0]) for every lookup inside the tick; writes still go through bus.update. Replace the in-loop
   bus.read(...) calls in daemon.py and planner_runs.py with snapshot lookups. A stage that must see its own writes
   re-reads only the task it changed (bus.get).
3. Hot set: bus.read() skips archived tasks. Tasks that are done/merged/superseded/failed and older than 7 days (by
   updated time or last event), and whose goal is closed, move to .orchestrator/tasks/archive/ (a move, never a delete; a
   bus.get of an archived id still works by falling back to the archive path).
4. Timing log: `[daemon] slow stage <name> <s>s` for any tick stage over 5 s and a tick total over 30 s.
Acceptance targets on this repo's real data (copy .orchestrator/tasks to a temp dir for the measurement): bus.read() under
0.3 s; one full tick with spawning stubbed under 15 s.
Tests (tests/test_bus.py, tests/test_daemon.py): test_read_takes_lock_once, test_tick_uses_one_snapshot (count bus.read
calls per tick == 1), test_archive_moves_old_closed_tasks_and_get_still_finds_them, test_slow_stage_is_logged.
Run: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_bus tests.test_daemon tests.test_planner_runs. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: bus.read() under 0.3 s on a copy of this repo's 1725 tasks
a full tick on the copy under 15 s with spawning stubbed
old closed tasks archived by move; bus.get still finds them

result.summary:
Everything is committed on `task/T-1726` (260d87a and e3f248b) and the tree is clean. All four named tests pass, as do the full `tests.test_bus`, `tests.test_daemon` and `tests.test_planner_runs` modules. Two of the performance targets are only met once the first tick has run, so read the timings below.

**What changed**
- **Locking:** `bus.read()` now takes the bus lock once for the whole scan instead of once per task (`test_read_takes_lock_once` checks it is one call).
- **Atomic writes:** `_save` now writes a temp file and renames it, so a reader never sees a half-written task.
- **Parse cache:** `bus.read()` reuses its last parse of a file until the file changes. Parsing took most of the read time: the remaining 426 tasks add up to 39 MB, and T-1378 alone is 20 MB of events. One catch: callers get their own copy of the task's top level, but nested values are shared with the cache and must not be changed in place.
- **One read per tick:** `tick()` reads the bus once into `bus.snapshot()`, and every later `bus.read()` in that tick is answered from memory, including calls from other modules. Writes still go through `bus.update` and show up in the snapshot. A new `bus.children(tid, role)` replaces the five in-loop "find reviews for this task" scans. Writes from other processes show up on the next tick.
- **Archive:** each tick moves closed tasks (done, merged, superseded, failed) to `.orchestrator/tasks/archive/` once they are untouched for 7 days and their parent goal is done. They are moved, never deleted. `bus.get` and `next_id` still look in the archive. Goal tasks themselves are never archived, because ship needs to see closed goals.
- **Timing log:** `[daemon] slow stage <name> <s>s` for any stage over 5 s, and `[daemon] slow tick <s>s` for a tick over 30 s.
- **`planner_runs.py`:** `build_ctx` now asks for children by parent, and the per-decision "fix round already in flight?" check scans once instead of once per decision.

**Measured on a copy of the 1726 tasks** (spawning, merging, the gate and the planner launch stubbed)

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bus.read()` | 2.1–3.1 s | 0.30 s on the first read in a fresh process, 0.02–0.05 s after that |
| Full tick | not re-measured; minutes in the field | 17.5 s for the first tick, then 6–12.5 s |
| Disk scans per tick | many | 1 |

- **First tick:** the 17.5 s includes the one-time archive of 1300 tasks (1.4 s) and the first full parse. That one is over the 15 s target; every later tick is under it.
- **First read:** 0.30 s sits right at the 0.3 s target. Later reads are well under it.

Most of a warm tick is now outside this task's write scope: `harness_depth.history_table` through `scorecard.efficiency` takes about 4 s, and `pool.config()` is re-parsed about 100 times per tick (about 1.5 s).

**Files changed**
- `orchestrator/bus.py`
- `orchestrator/daemon.py`
- `orchestrator/planner_runs.py`
- `tests/test_bus.py`
- `tests/test_daemon.py`

No new dependencies.
